symbols.name: _walk
symbols.doc: Every (path, key, value) in a JSON body.

symbols.name: test_no_field_could_suppress_a_pane
symbols.doc: The strong form: there is no boolean anywhere under ``panes``.

symbols.name: test_the_comparison_is_over_the_whole_result_not_the_page
symbols.doc: B25. The page is 50; the comparison is 8,400.

symbols.name: test_a_disagreement_carries_both_panes_the_count_and_the_index
symbols.doc: The pick response's four required parts, on the pick that has a real disagreement to report (walkthrough step 11).

symbols.name: test_a_disagreement_past_the_page_is_still_on_the_page
symbols.doc: B25's D8: *a disagreement is never below the fold of a paginator.* Driven with a synthetic pair rather than a real pick, because no seeded pick disagrees past row 50 — and the rule has to hold when one does.

symbols.name: test_it_shows_both_probes_including_the_one_that_did_not_run
symbols.doc: B30: *the statement and both probes open, in full, with the probe that did not run stated in a comment rather than hidden.*

symbols.name: test_it_states_both_pinned_session_values
symbols.doc: AC-26's second half, and the reason it exists: each of these changes the answer, and neither is visible anywhere else.

symbols.name: test_the_pinned_values_are_what_the_connection_actually_ran_at
symbols.doc: The pane's claim, checked against the database rather than against the constant it was rendered from.

symbols.name: test_an_accepted_alias_is_shown_exactly_as_it_was_emitted
symbols.doc: §9.3: the one piece of user-typed text in the statement that is not a bind parameter, double-quoted, visible.

symbols.name: test_a_layer_1_refusal_says_there_is_no_sql_and_shows_none
symbols.doc: §9.3's refusal half, and AC-16's *both panes empty*.

symbols.name: test_a_layer_2_refusal_names_the_probe_and_sends_nothing
symbols.doc: §4.5: SQL existed, the probe fired, the statement never ran.

symbols.name: test_the_reported_fallback_really_does_render_pythons_rows
symbols.doc: The same refusal with rows behind it, so §4.5's *"the Python pane shows Python's answer"* is watched producing some.

symbols.name: _Recorder
symbols.doc: A connection that answers exactly like the real one and remembers every statement text handed to the driver.

symbols.name: _RecordingCursor
symbols.doc: The same spy, one level down, on the cursor the SQL pane executes on.

symbols.name: test_the_display_rendering_never_reaches_the_driver
symbols.doc: AC-27, at the boundary.

symbols.name: test_the_sort_slots_field_name_is_bound_and_not_written
symbols.doc: The sort slot's half of AC-28, on a name the slot may hold.

symbols.name: test_a_hostile_field_name_in_the_sort_slot_is_refused_by_name
symbols.doc: W13-2, and the reason the test above uses an ordinary name.

symbols.name: test_every_slot_spelling_the_two_panes_would_split_on_is_refused
symbols.doc: The fence, over each slot that holds a field, not just the sort.

symbols.name: test_the_row_count_is_unaffected
symbols.doc: AC-28's second half. The field does not exist on any row, so reading it changes nothing about which rows come back — which is what it means for the name to have stayed out of the SQL.

symbols.name: test_the_alias_is_the_one_piece_of_typed_text_that_is_not_bound
symbols.doc: The criterion's own carve-out, stated as a test so it is not read as an oversight: a column name has no parameter position, so §4.10's allowlist governs it instead — and refuses this one.

symbols.name: test_every_visitor_gets_the_same_nine_controls
symbols.doc: §9.4: no author/viewer split, no permission gate, no saved view.

symbols.name: TestABadRequestIsAnswered
symbols.doc: DR-2's rule for the pick body, applied to the two routes that take a pick in the query string.

symbols.name: TestAllNineOperationsAreReachable
symbols.doc: AC-25, in the one place the nine controls are decided (B22).

symbols.name: test_every_operation_is_reachable_from_the_initial_pick
symbols.doc: Reachable means: enabled on the screen's own opening state, or enabled by a pick a person can make from it. Nothing is reachable only by editing JSON.

symbols.name: test_operation_7_offers_exactly_two_granularities
symbols.doc: Q20's own option text, and no week, month or free-text unit.

symbols.name: test_operation_8_offers_a_field_and_nothing_else
symbols.doc: R14: width 3, trailing, arithmetic mean are all FIXED — so there is deliberately no width box, no direction switch and no second aggregate. AC-25 tests exactly this absence.

symbols.name: test_operation_9_offers_a_toggle_and_no_picker
symbols.doc: R13 and AC-40(e): an on/off toggle is the only control, and there must be no picker for what it compares.

symbols.name: test_the_screen_renders_no_control_the_contract_did_not_serve
symbols.doc: B22 point 2, asserted structurally against ``pick.jsx``.

symbols.name: test_the_built_bundle_renders_that_note
symbols.doc: The absence leaves no trace unless it is drawn, so the note has to survive into the page a person actually loads.

symbols.name: test_the_built_bundle_prints_both_of_them_side_by_side
symbols.doc: They live NOWHERE else on the screen (§9.3), which is the whole reason AC-43(d) is a separate part: the time zone is what makes a day's bucket seven and not eight, and nothing else on the page would tell a reader what it was.

symbols.name: TestTheTwoSprites
symbols.doc: The day GIMS adds an ``i-sort`` of its own, this fails — rather than the demo silently shadowing it.

symbols.name: test_the_resolvers_two_lists_match_the_two_sprite_files
symbols.doc: The resolver decides from a literal list, so the list has to be the file. Parsed rather than imported: there is no JavaScript runtime in this suite, and there must not need to be (AC-36).

symbols.name: test_the_vendored_sprite_is_checked_first
symbols.doc: B17: i-play, i-plus and i-search exist in both drawings with different path data, and GIMS's shapes are the ones that render.

symbols.name: TestDemoCssIsNotAForkOfWatery
symbols.doc: The one assertion that keeps a silent copy of GIMS's stylesheet out of the demo. The approved mock inlines a near-copy of watery's ``:root`` because a mock has to be a single file; copying that block into demo.css would defeat D1's drift check completely, because a fragment cannot be checksummed against its source.

symbols.name: test_demo_css_declares_no_custom_property_at_all
symbols.doc: Stronger than B18's own grep, and for the same reason: moving the fork off ``:root`` would still be a fork.

symbols.name: test_demo_css_does_not_redefine_waterys_own_primitives
symbols.doc: Part 5.1's reused-unchanged list. A rule for any of these here would be a restyle of GIMS's components under another name.

symbols.name: test_these_two_files_alone_are_off_host_clean
symbols.doc: A NARROW check, and it says so — it is NOT the AC-32 guard.

symbols.name: TestTheBundlesAreCommitted
symbols.doc: A bundle that exists on the build machine and not in a fresh clone is the worst shape a criterion can have: AC-36 would pass here and fail for everyone else. ``.gitignore`` ignores ``dist/`` and ``build/`` at any depth, which is exactly why the bundles are written to ``demo/static/js/``.

symbols.name: TestTheBundleIsNotStale
symbols.doc: Someone edits a .jsx and forgets ``./run-demo build-ui``, so the screen a reviewer sees is not the screen the source describes. ``build-ui`` records a sha256 over the concatenated sources in ``demo/manifest.json``; this recomputes it.

symbols.name: TestTheScreenCannotHideEitherPane
symbols.doc: AC-20 read as a property of the built page rather than of the API: ``.pane-pair`` carries no collapse affordance, and there is nothing on the screen that could suppress one side.

symbols.name: test_the_frame_goes_coral_only_when_they_differ
symbols.doc: DR-1's second of three independent signals, and D3's one named exception to Watery's role table.

symbols.name: test_the_verdict_carries_words_and_an_icon_and_not_only_colour
symbols.doc: DR-1.3: AGREE and DISAGREE differ in WORDS and ICONS, so the banner is legible in greyscale and to a red/green-confused reader.

symbols.name: TestTheDataSaysItIsInventedInThreePlaces
symbols.doc: B31. (1) the masthead chip and the standing banner, as drawn; (2) one ``.chip.warn`` reading ``invented`` in EACH answer pane's head — the one addition this build makes to the approved drawing, because a screenshot of the panes alone carries neither of the other two; (3) the seed script's own header and console line, which ``test_data.py`` asserts.

symbols.name: TestTheSevenStatesAreReachable
symbols.doc: The approved mock draws seven artboards. The built screen keeps the mock's own tab strip and makes it real: a tab loads that state's pick INTO the nine controls and runs it against the database. So "reachable" is not a claim about a drawing — every one of the seven is a pick this suite runs, and what comes back is what the mock's view says comes back.

symbols.name: test_the_disagreement_state_is_located_and_not_merely_announced
symbols.doc: D8, and the one view the whole design is arranged around.

symbols.name: test_the_bucketed_state_disables_more_than_the_mock_drew
symbols.doc: B5a greys one more control on the bucketed view than the drawing does — operation 9 as well as 4 and 8. It is one of exactly two places this build exceeds the approved drawing, it comes from the legality matrix rather than from the screen, and it is named here so it cannot become a surprise.
